_comment: DYST PER-FILE sidecar template. Copy this file next to a media file and rename it to match the media's base name (e.g. media/videos/scare.mp4 -> media/videos/scare.json), then edit the values you want. A .txt form is also supported (one `key=value` per line). Only the keys you set override the global config.json values; keys you leave out fall back to config.json (or its defaults). Delete a key to stop overriding it. The _comment/_example_sidecar/_hints/_hints_deprecated blocks are ignored by the app — they are documentation only. All per-file keys and how each interacts with the global config.json key are listed in _hints below.

_hints.image_display_seconds: How long THIS image/animation stays up (seconds). Overrides the global `image_display_seconds` and takes PRIORITY over the per-file `duration` alias when both are present. Ignored by videos (they run to their end unless `max_duration` caps them). Supports randomization: a "min~max" string (e.g. "0.5~1.5") draws a new value every trigger; both bounds must be valid.
_hints.duration: Per-file alias for `image_display_seconds`: how long THIS image/GIF stays up (seconds). Video ignores it. Interacts with `image_display_seconds` (that key wins if both are set), `end_on_audio_end` (the timer is ignored when that is true and a sidecar audio exists) and `max_duration` (the hard cap always wins). Supports randomization: a "min~max" string (e.g. "0.5~1.5") draws a new value every trigger; both bounds must be valid.
_hints.end_on_audio_end: IMAGES/GIFs only: true = THIS image IGNORES its display time and stays up until its sidecar audio ENDS, then fades out. No sidecar audio = no effect (normal timer runs). Overrides the global `end_on_audio_end`. `max_duration` still applies and wins over a long audio track.
_hints.fade_in_seconds: Fade-in (seconds) for THIS image/GIF before the display clock starts: opacity 0 -> `opacity`. Videos ignore it. Overrides the global `fade_in_seconds`. Lifetime = fade_in + display + fade_out. `speed` divides all three. Supports randomization: a "min~max" string (e.g. "0.5~1.5") draws a new value every trigger; both bounds must be valid.
_hints.fade_out_seconds: Fade-out (seconds) for THIS image/GIF. Videos end instantly (no fade). Overrides the global `fade_out_seconds`. The old name `fade_seconds` is still accepted as a deprecated alias. 0 = instant. Supports randomization: a "min~max" string (e.g. "0.5~1.5") draws a new value every trigger; both bounds must be valid.
_hints.max_duration: Hard cap (seconds) for THIS media AND its audio. When it fires, the visual + audio stop immediately, with NO fade-out, and the overlay closes. Overrides the global `max_duration`; a per-file 0 explicitly DISABLES a global cap for this file. 0 = no cap. Supports ranges: "1.0~5.0".
_hints.speed: Playback speed multiplier for THIS media (> 0): scales video frame rate + own audio, GIF animation, sidecar audio, and image display time + fades (all timings / speed). Overrides the global `speed`, but is OVERRIDDEN by `speed_pitch` when that is > 0 (per-file > global). Default 1. Supports ranges: "1.0~2.0".
_hints.pitch: Audio pitch multiplier for THIS media (> 0), independent of speed (the audio is re-encoded via ffmpeg; needs ffmpeg when != 1). Overrides the global `pitch`, but is OVERRIDDEN by `speed_pitch` when that is > 0. Default 1. Supports ranges: "0.5~1.5".
_hints.speed_pitch: Combined speed+pitch for THIS media (>= 0): when > 0 it sets BOTH `speed` and `pitch` to this value and OVERRIDES the individual `speed`/`pitch` keys (per-file AND global). 0 = off (use speed/pitch separately). Per-file value wins over the global `speed_pitch`. Default 0. Supports ranges: "1.0~2.0".
_hints.max_playback_height: Performance cap (px) for THIS file: taller sources are downscaled (aspect kept) BEFORE decode/chroma-key/copy/paint. Videos + GIFs; still images ignore it. Overrides the global `max_playback_height`; 0 = no cap. Changing it rebuilds that file's precache.
_hints.max_playback_fps: Framerate cap for THIS video: frames above it are sampled (duration and audio untouched). GIFs ignore it. Overrides the global `max_playback_fps`; 0 = no cap. Changing it rebuilds that file's precache.
_hints.volume: Volume multiplier for THIS media (0.0-5.0). MULTIPLIES the global `volume`: final = global * per-file, so 0.5 halves it and 2 doubles it (per-file does NOT replace global). Ignored when the file has no audio. Default 1. Supports randomization: a "min~max" string (e.g. "0.5~1.5") draws a new value every trigger; both bounds must be valid.
_hints.mode: How THIS media covers the screen: fit (default, whole media visible, aspect kept) | stretch (squish to screen) | cover-height (fit screen width, crop top/bottom) | cover-width (fit screen height, crop left/right) | custom (use the custom-mode keys below). Overrides the global `mode`. The removed 'cover' value falls back to 'fit'.
_hints.opacity: Overlay transparency for THIS media (0.0-1.0; 1 = fully opaque). Overrides the global `opacity`. Fades compose on top (fade-in 0 -> opacity, fade-out opacity -> 0). Supports randomization: a "min~max" string (e.g. "0.5~1.5") draws a new value every trigger; both bounds must be valid.
_hints.position_x: Custom mode only: horizontal placement for THIS media, clamped to -1..2 (0 = left edge at the screen's left edge, 1 = right edge at the right edge, 0.5 = centered; outside 0..1 peeks/crops off-screen). Overrides the global `position_x`. Ignored unless `mode` is custom. Supports ranges: "-0.5~1.5".
_hints.position_y: Custom mode only: vertical placement for THIS media, clamped to -1..2 (0 = top edge at the screen's top edge, 1 = bottom edge at the bottom edge, 0.5 = centered; outside 0..1 peeks/crops off-screen). Overrides the global `position_y`. Ignored unless `mode` is custom. Supports ranges: "-0.5~1.5".
_hints.scale_x: Custom mode only: width multiplier for THIS media relative to the aspect-preserving 'fit' size (1 = whole media visible). Overrides the global `scale_x`. IMPORTANT: giving BOTH per-file `scale_x` AND `scale_y` OVERWRITES the per-file `scale`; a lone `scale_x`/`scale_y` overrides only its own axis. Ignored unless `mode` is custom. Supports ranges: "0.5~1.5".
_hints.scale_y: Custom mode only: height multiplier for THIS media relative to the 'fit' size. Overrides the global `scale_y`. See `scale_x` for how it interacts with `scale` / `scale_x`. Ignored unless `mode` is custom. Supports ranges: "0.5~1.5".
_hints.scale: Custom mode only (per-file only; there is no global `scale`): a uniform scale for THIS media that sets BOTH axes to the same value (e.g. 2 = twice as wide AND twice as tall). OVERWRITTEN when BOTH `scale_x` AND `scale_y` are given in the same sidecar; a lone `scale_x`/`scale_y` overrides only its own axis. A range ("0.5~1.5") draws ONE random value shared by both axes, so X and Y always match. Ignored unless `mode` is custom.
_hints.flip_h: Custom mode only: mirror THIS media horizontally (true/false; "random" picks a random bool each trigger). Overrides the global `flip_h`. Ignored unless `mode` is custom.
_hints.flip_v: Custom mode only: mirror THIS media vertically (true/false; "random" picks a random bool each trigger). Overrides the global `flip_v`. Ignored unless `mode` is custom.
_hints.rotation: Custom mode only: rotation in degrees for THIS media, around its own center (any number). Overrides the global `rotation`. Ignored unless `mode` is custom. Supports ranges: "0~360".
_hints.weight: Pick likelihood relative to all other media (>= 0, floats allowed; default 1): chance = weight / total_weight. 2 = twice as likely as a weight-1 file, 0.5 = half, 0 = NEVER picked (a warning is logged at scan). Works in ANY mode. Not shown in the top-level keys above only because it defaults to 1; add it to a sidecar to change it.
_hints.play_once: true = THIS media cannot be selected again while any copy of it is already playing. false = repeats are allowed. Overrides the global `play_once`. Default false.
_hints.chroma: Per-file ON/OFF gate for chroma-key removal: true = filter THIS file using the global (or per-file) preset, false = SKIP filtering even when the global `chroma_key` is on (use it for assets that already have real alpha, or normal videos). `false` ALWAYS wins over a preset. Works in ANY mode. Omitted from the top-level keys above so copying this template does not force keying on; add it to a sidecar when needed.
_hints.chroma_key:
Per-file chroma PRESET for THIS media: 'green' | 'blue' | 'weak green' | 'strong green' | 'weak blue' | 'strong blue' | 'black' | 'white' | 'custom'. Uses its own key independently of the global `chroma_key`, so one file can be blue-screened while the rest are green. Setting any preset turns keying ON for this file; a per-file `chroma: false` still wins and skips keying entirely. NOT randomizable.
PRESETS:
 • green - hue 35..85, sat 40..255, val 40..255 (window midpoint = hue 60; the everyday green screen)
 • weak green - hue 28..92, sat 20..255, val 30..255 (much WIDER hue + accepts faint/dull screen: for uneven, dim, over-lit or spill-heavy backdrops)
 • strong green - hue 42..78, sat 60..255, val 50..255 (NARROWER hue + must be more saturated/brighter: vivid, evenly lit screens, safest against a greenish subject)
 • blue - hue 100..130, sat 40..255, val 40..255 (midpoint = hue 115)
 • weak blue - hue 90..145, sat 20..255, val 30..255 (wider/fainter, blue equivalent of weak green)
 • strong blue - hue 105..130, sat 60..255, val 50..255
 • black - LUMA mode (hue/sat ignored): keys dark pixels, val 0..35, whatever their colour — a dark backdrop instead of a colour screen
 • white - LUMA mode (hue ignored): keys bright AND desaturated pixels, val 220..255 with sat 0..30 — a white/lightbox backdrop
 • custom - ignores every preset above and uses the chroma_hue_range / chroma_saturation_range / chroma_value_range windows instead
Omitted from the top-level keys above so copying this template does not force keying on; see _example_sidecar.

How the numbers work (OpenCV HSV, NOT the 0-360/0-100 you may know from an image editor): HUE is 0..179 because it is degrees halved (0/179 = red, 60 = green, 115 = blue), SATURATION is 0..255 = how vivid the colour is (0 = grey/white/black), VALUE is 0..255 = pixel brightness. The ranges are not pass/fail switches: the hue range is a WINDOW that keys hardest at its MIDPOINT (lo+hi)/2 and fades out by (hi-lo)/2 either side (wrapping at 0/179), while the sat/val LOW bound is a floor (pixels below it are never keyed) and their HIGH bound is stored but unused for colour keying. The midpoint of the hue window also picks which spill colour despill strips (midpoints 35-85 = green, 100-130 = blue, <=15 or >=160 = red). The mask is then eroded, hole-filled and feathered. Videos are auto-calibrated: at precache time the hue midpoint is re-measured from the clip's own border pixels, so for video only the hue WIDTH is really yours to tune.
_hints.chroma_hue_range: Per-file custom-chroma Custom-chroma HUE window [lo, hi]. OpenCV hue 0..179 — it is degrees HALVED, so 0/179 = red, 60 = green, 115 = blue (NOT 0-360, and NOT the 0-100 of some editors). Used ONLY when `chroma_key` is 'custom' (or the expert dict uses preset 'custom'); it is ignored for every named preset and ignored in luma/black/white mode. It is a WINDOW, not a pass/fail cut: the mask keys hardest at the MIDPOINT (lo+hi)/2 and fades out by (hi-lo)/2 either side, wrapping around at 0/179. That means only the midpoint and the WIDTH matter — [50, 70] and [55, 75] behave identically apart from the shift — and the WIDTH is what you tune: narrow it (e.g. 50..70) when a greenish/bluish subject keeps getting punched out, widen it (e.g. 25..95) when the backdrop's hue drifts or is unevenly lit. For VIDEOS the midpoint is auto-calibrated to the clip's real screen colour at precache time, so only the width has an effect there. The midpoint also selects which spill colour despill removes (35-85 green, 100-130 blue, <=15 or >=160 red).
_hints.chroma_saturation_range: Per-file custom-chroma Custom-chroma SATURATION window [lo, hi]. OpenCV saturation 0..255 = how VIVID the pixel colour is (0 = grey/white/black = no colour at all, 255 = fully saturated). In colour mode ONLY the LOW bound does anything: pixels below `lo` are never keyed (the gate is (sat - lo)/(255 - lo)), which protects dull/greyish subject pixels from being eaten. Raise `lo` (e.g. 80-120) when washed-out or whitish parts of the subject keep disappearing; lower it (e.g. 15-30) when a faded/pale screen leaves a grey-green ghost behind. The HIGH bound is stored but unused by the colour mask — it only acts as a mode detector (a hi <= 30 switches the keyer into luma/black/white mode). Only the LOW number is worth editing. Default [40, 255]. Used ONLY with the 'custom' preset.
_hints.chroma_value_range: Per-file custom-chroma Custom-chroma VALUE window [lo, hi]. OpenCV value 0..255 = pixel BRIGHTNESS (the largest of the R/G/B channels), 0 = black, 255 = fully lit. In colour mode ONLY the LOW bound does anything: pixels darker than `lo` are treated as shadow and forced to alpha 0 (never keyed). Raise `lo` (e.g. 60-90) when dark, shadowed parts of the screen — or dark subject areas — keep getting keyed out; lower it (e.g. 15-25) when the screen is dim or lit unevenly with dark corners. The HIGH bound is stored but unused for colour keying; it drives the mode detector (hi <= 60 or lo >= 200 selects the luma keyer used by the 'black'/'white' presets, where it becomes the actual keying threshold). Default [40, 255]. Used ONLY with the 'custom' preset.

_hints_deprecated: OLD/REMOVED keys: 'fade_seconds' renamed to 'fade_out_seconds' (old name still accepted as a deprecated alias); the global 'cover' mode was removed (falls back to 'fit'); per-file 'chroma' is now a true/false ON/OFF gate, while 'chroma_key' is the per-file PRESET string.
